correctness.rationale: Conditional on |S|=s, the loss is at least f_H(s). Its convex minorant and Jensen therefore bound the objective below by ell_H(nq). The lower hull is the optimum of a finite mixture of cardinalities at fixed mean nq, attained with at most two cardinalities. Given a minimizer at each, uniform group translation yields marginal s/n at cardinality s by transitivity and preserves the cost, including for equivariant multiplicities, so the bound is attained. This covers q=0 and q=1 as deterministic endpoints. On a cycle 2s=2e(S)+boundary and boundary is at most 2 min(s,n-s). Independent sets attain the zero part and their complements attain the dense part of max(0,2s-n), including n=3. Integer slopes 0,1,2 for odd n and 0,2 for even n give the interpolation and excess over the summed Frechet bound. The introductory dependence statement should be read as 'in general': q=0,1 or all singleton hyperedges give expectation fixed by marginals, while otherwise perfect coupling and independence give different expectations. No exception to the stated sharp theorem is needed. The finite checker was inspected, not run.
residual_risks: The optimization is over all laws, not a model of which dependence structures occur ecologically. The hull reduction does not make the hypergraph profile computationally easy.

value.rationale: Dependence is a meaningful modeling issue, but the demonstrated explicit cycle invariant is already mechanically supplied by a published convex hull. The remaining general result performs ordinary group averaging and one-dimensional convexification and leaves the underlying hypergraph extremal profile unevaluated. No additional nonroutine hypergraph case or scientifically distinct consequence is demonstrated to make a viable standalone repair of this record.
residual_risks: New evaluations for other motivated incidence families may have independent value; none is claimed here.
